memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But the Lord inflicted serious diseases on Pharaoh and his household because of Abram's wife Sarai. So Pharaoh summoned Abram. "What have you done to me?" he said. "Why didn't you tell me she was my wife?" - Gen 12:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abram failed, but God did not. When Abram would not protect his wife, God did. He intervened directly, striking Pharaoh's household, to rescue Sarai and safeguard the promise. Notice who acts here: not Abram, who created the mess, but God, who cleans it up.

This is grace in action. Abram had done nothing to deserve rescue. His scheme was cowardly, his lie was self-serving, and he had endangered the very woman through whom God's promise would come. Yet God stepped in - not because Abram earned it, but because God had made a promise and He keeps His promises.

Notice the humiliation in the scene: a pagan king rebukes God's chosen man. "What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me?" Abram has nothing to say. He stands silent while an unbeliever teaches him about honesty. Our sin often shames us before people who should be learning from us.

But the deeper truth here is glorious. God's purposes do not rest on our reliability. He protects His promises even from the failures of His own people. Paul says it plainly: "he who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion" (Phil 1:6). When your failures threaten to derail everything, remember: God is more committed to His promise than you are, and He will see it through.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Can you see times God protected you from your own bad decisions?
- Does your confidence rest on your reliability or God's faithfulness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Faithful God, thank You that Your promises do not depend on my reliability. Thank You for the times You rescued me from my own failures. My confidence rests in Your faithfulness, not mine.
Amen.
